doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

title: Young Cuban women musicians, their parents and Cuba's love of music
summary: Parents were generally supportive; everyone in Cuba has opinions about music. She first went around 1981-82.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you were, I don’t know if it’s recruiting if I can use that word — young women to fulfill your vision was there a question about like what did their parents think of this idea, did you describe the life of a musician — here’s what you’re getting into?

No, not at all. I just hoped that their parents wouldn’t get in the way and try and stop it, but generally, you know Cubans love music and you know it’s so deep in peoples’ lives. That that’s one of the things I’ve loved so much about Cuba is everybody loves music. And if you’re a musician they sort of welcome you with open arms. And any person, you know if it could be somebody working in a restaurant or driving a cab, like all the people know their music and know the musicians and have their opinions on who’s good and who’s bad. It’s not like in North America where you could ask somebody what their favorite song is and they’re like, “I don’t know” or ask them a musical question, “Who do you think are the best ten such-and-such.” People say, “I don’t know.” “What’s your favorite music?” “I don’t know.” But there everybody has an opinion and is passionate about music. So the parents are, generally the parents are pretty, have been pretty down and involved in making it happen for them.
When did you, if you’ll remind me when you first went over there.
